trial_court: Court of the Judge, Family Court, Jajpur (C.P. No.106 of 2015) and Bhubaneswar (Civil Proceeding No.222 of 2013)
case_name: Namita Mohananda vs Tripati Mohananda — TRP(C) No.148 of 2017
facts_of_case: Petitioner-wife seeks transfer of C.P. No.106 of 2015 filed under Section 13(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 read with Section 7 of the Family Courts Act, 1984 from Jajpur to Bhubaneswar due to difficulty in appearing on each date of posting.

legal_principles.principle: Notice on the opposite party is held to be sufficient.
legal_principles.held: In view of such submission made and office note, so also Judgments of the Supreme Court reported in AIR 1989 SC 630 (M/s. Madan & Co. Vs. Wazir Jaivir Chand), in (1999) 7 SCC 510 (K. Bhaskaran Vs. Sankaran Vaidhyan Balan & anr.), in (2006) 6 SCC 456 (D. Vinod Shivappa Vs. Nanda Belliappa), in (2007) 6 SCC 555 (C.C. Alivi Haji Vs. Palapetty Muhammed & anr.) and in (2014) 12 SCC 685 (Ajeet Seeds Limited Vs. K. Gopal Krishnaiah), notice on the Opposite Party is held to be sufficient.

legal_principles.principle: Interest of justice would be best served if the case is transferred.
legal_principles.held: Interest of justice would be best served if C.P. No.106 of 2015 is transferred to the Court of the Judge, Family Court, Bhubaneswar, where C.P. No.222 of 2013 filed at the instance of the petitioner-wife is stated to be pending, for disposal in accordance with law.

outcome.final_order: Notice is held to be sufficient and the case is transferred to the Court of the Judge, Family Court, Bhubaneswar.

use_for_drafting: drafting a transfer petition for divorce case
advising on residence and appearance in family courts
preparing a case for transfer of proceedings
